method: Independent lens review of captured evidence. The director opened every screenshot for a surface before scoring it, read the axe and capture results, and scored without sight of any other director's scores.
overallNote: Through the journey and task-success lens this baseline is good, considered work that has not yet closed its loops. The strongest signal is that plain-language scaffolding is already systemic, not decorative: the Tasks board explains every column in a sentence, due states are relative rather than raw dates, Notes states 'Private to you' before you ask, and Timeline discloses 'Anyone holding the link can read it' before the Share button is pressed. That is real first-contact discipline and it is why nothing here scores below 7.4. What holds every surface off the 9.5 floor is the same pattern repeating: the path is legible right up to the moment of action, then stops being shown. The board explains its columns but never shows how to move a card out of one. Notes builds an excellent triage loop but only offers 'Turn into task' on rows already flagged for review. Timeline counts down to a wedding day its axis stops short of labelling. Pricing describes four ways in without putting a price or a CTA on the first screen, and the marketing nav has no Sign in at either viewport, so a returning user has no visible door. Task detail is dense with capable controls whose names hide their outcomes — 'Make copies', 'open source', 'Draft a reply'. Separately, one straightforward defect: the desktop List view clips its priority column mid-word at 1440. I have issued no veto — axe is clean across all sixteen captures, there are no console errors, every path returned 200, and each of these is a recoverable gap rather than a blocked user. I want to be explicit about what this evidence cannot support: drag-and-drop on the board, the Share flow past the button, the guest view, motion, and any mutation path are all unexercised by static captures, and I have given them no optimism in these scores.

surfaces.rationale: The board does the single best novice thing I saw anywhere: every column carries a one-line explainer under its title — 'Agreed and ready to start.', 'In motion right now.', 'Being checked before it goes out.', 'Held by a reply, a delivery, or a decision.', 'Finished work stays visible.' — and the empty Waiting column says 'Nothing held up.' Due states are relative and human ('Due today', 'Overdue by 2 days' in red, 'Milestone due 1 Aug') rather than bare dates, and 'Unscheduled' in List is plainer than any competitor's em-dash. Against that, three things break the unaided path. First, the desktop List view overflows at 1440: the rightmost column header renders as 'P…' and its values as 'Hig' / 'Low' / 'No…', literally cut mid-word at the viewport edge with no visible horizontal-scroll affordance — the priority column is unreadable at the default width. Second, each List row carries two adjacent unlabelled controls, a square select checkbox and a round complete circle, and nothing distinguishes 'tick this to finish it' from 'tick this to select it'. Third, the board offers no visible way to move a card between columns: no grip, no per-card menu on desktop, no hint that dragging is the mechanic — and static captures cannot prove drag works or is discoverable, so I am giving it no credit. 'Planning · 5 undated' and 'Day 11 of 97' in the header are both unexplained shorthand. Mobile handles the width honestly with a column-chip jumper (To do 3, In progress 3, Review 2, Waiting 0) above horizontally scrolling columns, though the peeking second column truncates mid-word.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Stop the desktop List table clipping the priority column at 1440 — either fit the columns to the viewport or give the table its own horizontal scroll with a visible edge affordance, so 'Hig' / 'Low' / 'No…' read as whole words.

surfaces.rationale: The core job — understand a task and finish it — is well served: 'Mark done' is the unmissable primary action, status / owner / due date / priority sit in one row at the top on both viewports, and the empty states teach rather than apologise ('No conversation yet. Comments and changes will appear here as they happen.', 'Drop files here, or paste a link…'). The SOURCE block tracing back to the originating note and quoting the approved wording is a genuine trust move I rarely see. But several controls are opaque to someone who has never used a project tool. 'From Notes · open source' collides head-on with the software term — it means 'open the source note' and will be misread by everyone, on a journey-critical link. 'COPIES → Make copies' names no outcome: duplicate this task, how many, where? 'ADD FIELD → + Amount' offers exactly one option under a generic header, so a novice cannot tell whether Amount is the only field that exists. 'DRAFT A REPLY' with a sparkle sits beside the comment box with no indication whether it posts or drafts for review — an unlabelled AI action at the point of writing to another person. The status pill 'To do' is styled flatter than its neighbours 'No due date' and 'High', so it reads as a label rather than an editable control. On mobile the whole metadata rail is pushed below the entire conversation block, so Repeats / Tags / Contact arrive only after a long scroll, and the five icon controls crammed into the 390px header are small and unlabelled.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Rewrite the opaque controls in outcome language — 'open source' → 'Open the note this came from', 'Make copies' → 'Duplicate this task', and make clear whether 'Draft a reply' writes for you to edit or posts.

surfaces.rationale: This is the clearest journey in the app. The composer prompt 'Write the thought before it disappears…' states the job in one line, the three capture modes (Type / Voice / Photo) are visible rather than buried, and 'Private to you' answers the first anxious question before it is asked. The triage loop is the strongest piece of interaction design in the set: notes needing a decision surface Keep / Turn into task / Delete inline in the list, on exactly those rows, with chips ('To review', 'In Tasks') marking state — a novice can clear a backlog without being taught anything. The reading pane closes the loop with 'Captured 35 minutes ago · Edited 31 minutes ago' and a live link to the task the note became. Gaps: the relationship between Notebook 14 / Review 8 / In Tasks 6 must be inferred (8+6=14, never stated); the reading pane offers no 'Turn into task' of its own, so the conversion action exists only on list rows already flagged for review — a novice who writes a note and immediately wants it to become a task has no visible path; and the desktop reading pane is mostly empty white below a three-line note, which reads unfinished rather than calm. On mobile the tab counts are dropped and the active 'Notebook' pill bleeds flush to the left screen edge with no inset — a visible layout defect — and the sort control disappears, leaving only 'All notes'.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Put a 'Turn into task' action in the note reading pane for every note, not just rows already flagged 'To review', so the capture-to-execution path works from wherever the user is standing.

surfaces.rationale: The sharing state is handled better than most shipped products: 'Live since 15 Jul 2026. Anyone holding the link can read it.' sits above the fold in plain words, before the Share button is pressed, so nobody discovers the permission model after the fact. Relative time is used consistently and humanely — '79 days to go', 'in 16 days', 'Until wedding day / 79 days / 2 of 9 complete' — and milestone states are English, not jargon: Complete, Our next milestone, Coming up, Later. The break is the axis itself. Month ticks run Feb through Jul and then stop: everything right of 'Today' — the entire future, including the 3 Oct wedding day the page is counting down to — has no date scale at all. Four milestones on that side collapse into an unlabelled bracket reading '4 milestones', so a reader who has just been told '2 of 9 complete' can name five and cannot see the rest, with no visible way to expand them. 'Preview' and 'Share' sit adjacent with no indication that one shows the guest view. Mobile is the better adaptation — the axis becomes a vertical dated rail that is far more legible — but the capture cuts within two milestones so I cannot judge the full descent. What happens after Share is pressed (link creation, revoke, the guest's own view) is unexercised by this evidence and I have given it no credit.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Label the future half of the axis — carry month ticks through Aug/Sep/Oct and expand or make openable the collapsed '4 milestones' cluster, so the countdown and the axis tell the same story.

surfaces.rationale: The proposition lands in one read with zero jargon: 'Project management for people outside tech.' names the audience in the headline, and 'One calm system for people with work to manage, not software to manage' names the pain. The mono eyebrow 'NOTES → TASKS → TIMELINE' teaches the system's shape in five words, and the two CTAs are correctly graded — 'See the system at work ↓' is a scroll, not a commitment, and 'Join the waitlist →' carries the ask. Mobile keeps the hero intact and opens the narrative device 'ONE THREAD, THROUGH THE STUDIO / Follow one wedding…' below it. The journey break: there is no Sign in or account entry anywhere in the nav at either viewport — Products / Design / Pricing / About on desktop, Products plus a hamburger on mobile. A returning user who types the domain has no visible way into app.signalstudio.ie, and since Pricing names paying Pro and Enterprise tiers, that path has to exist for someone. Secondary: the entire first screen carries text only, with the right half empty, so a non-technical visitor asking 'what does it actually look like' is made to scroll for the answer; and 'Design' as a top-level nav item has an unguessable destination for a buyer.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Add a persistent Sign in entry to the marketing nav at both viewports so returning users can reach the signed-in app without guessing the subdomain.

surfaces.rationale: Judged on its actual job — convince a stranger this is for them, then send them somewhere — the writing does the heavy lifting well. 'Project management software was built by tech companies, for tech companies' is a thesis a novice grasps instantly, and the body earns it: it concedes that sprints, epics, backlogs, story points, stand-ups and retrospectives 'can all be useful when the work calls for them' before landing 'The mistake was assuming every project should work that way.' Naming jargon in order to disown it is exactly right for the first-contact standard. Mobile reads better than desktop and reaches the concrete anchor sooner — 'A wedding may be the largest project someone ever manages.' Desktop is the weaker journey: the headline sits left, the body column sits right and starts two-thirds down, and roughly a quarter of the first screen is an empty rectangle between them with no visual connector, so the eye has to hunt for where reading resumes. And within the captured region there is no onward step — no link to Pricing, no waitlist CTA — at the moment a persuaded reader is most ready to act. I cannot see below the fold, so I am scoring that as a first-screen observation rather than a claim about the whole page.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Bind the desktop headline and body into one reading path — close the empty quadrant between them — and give the persuaded reader an explicit next step on the page.

surfaces.rationale: The page most responsible for a decision defers the decision. Across both viewports, the first screen contains no price and no CTA: the headline 'One clear system. Four ways in.' announces four options and then delivers them as a run-on sentence — 'Start free, pay less while studying, move to Pro for ongoing work, or shape an Enterprise start with Ethan' — which a novice must parse to recover four plan names that ought to be four scannable things. A visitor has to scroll past a second headline ('Choose by the work in front of you.') before a number appears. The reassurance band is the best part: 'No charge / on the waitlist', 'VAT included / at the prevailing rate' are concrete and stack cleanly into ruled rows on mobile. But 'Terms repeated / before purchase' reads like a slip for 'restated', and 'Anything unresolved is named plainly' introduces the word 'unresolved' onto a pricing page, which raises a worry it does not then answer above the fold. 'Shape an Enterprise start with Ethan' names a person the visitor has never met with no visible link or role, so the enterprise path has no next action. Combined with the missing Sign in in the nav, a returning customer arriving here to check or change a plan has nowhere to go.
surfaces.highestLeverageFix: Bring the four plans and their prices onto the first screen as four scannable cards with a CTA each, rather than naming them inside a prose sentence above the fold.
